claims.text: The identity of X governs oxide stability by controlling where and how oxidation initiates.
Si preferentially segregates to the oxide/alloy interface.
Interfacial Si segregation accelerates formation of a thin, continuous, and adherent silicate or Si-rich oxide layer.
A Si-rich oxide layer accommodates thermal strain and minimizes oxide-growth stresses.
Mn tends to oxidize at the exposed alloy surface rather than at the oxide/alloy interface.
Al may, like Mn, tend to oxidize at the exposed alloy surface.
Mn-containing, and potentially Al-containing, alloys form thicker, less coherent, mechanically mismatched scales with inferior interfacial bonding.
The inferior scales proposed for Mn-containing and potentially Al-containing alloys are more prone to cracking and spallation.
The initial CrFeCoNiX alloys have a uniform distribution of all constituent elements.
Partitioning and segregation of X determine oxide nucleation location, scale continuity, and adhesion.
Oxide formation in high-entropy alloys reflects competing effects of kinetics, thermodynamics, chemistry, microstructure, stress, and environment.
Si has a relatively strong thermodynamic affinity for oxygen and can favor formation of a Si oxide.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX will retain a more stable and continuous protective scale than the Mn-containing variant during high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNi without X will form a heterogeneous mixed-oxide layer having behavior intermediate between the Si- and Mn-containing variants.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
The proposed behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Al is known to form protective Al2O3 in other alloy systems.
Si's effectiveness in promoting oxide adhesion is supported by prior evidence.

contradictions.description: The Al prediction is explicitly tentative and the uncertainty field allows protective Al2O3 behavior, yet an equally stable Al-containing scale is treated as a decisive falsifier. A result that the stated hypothesis partly allows should not independently falsify it.
